{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese Cuisine]]

'''Tempura''' is one of the fried foods of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japan]]. Various [[Cookbook:Meat|meats]], [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], and [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]] are dipped in [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] and then [[Cookbook:Deep-fat Frying|deep fried]] until lightly golden.

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] ice cold water
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]] for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep-frying]] ([[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]] is best)
* Meat, vegetables, or seafood
==Procedure==
# Heat oil in a deep pan to 340–350°F (~171–176°C).
# Beat the egg in a bowl and add ice cold water. Warmer water will produce a sticky batter and more oily tempura.
# Add flour and mix lightly. Do not overmix batter—a few lumps actually improve the result, adding crispiness.
# Dip meat or vegetables briefly in the batter, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] until brown.
# Remove from the oil and drain.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If using [[Cookbook:Shrimp|shrimp]], score them a few times crosswise on the underside, to prevent them from curling up during [[Cookbook:Deep-fat Frying|deep frying]]. Alternatively, [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] them before cooking. Remove the skewers before serving.
* You may also wish to include 1 tablespoon of [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] in the batter.
* Serve over white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] garnished with black [[Cookbook:Sesame Seed|sesame seeds]], in a bowl of [[Cookbook:Udon |udon noodle soup]], or in a bowl of [[Cookbook:Soba|soba noodle soup]]. Serving in [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] will make the cooked batter get mushy, of course.
